text:
maya: Heads-up — p99 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate jumped ~180ms right after we started the canary routing. UI shows route-level p99 up but endpoint p99 flat. anyone else see this?
jon: Saw it too. looks like canary traffic was routed to region-eu-2, but dashboard breakdown says sample_origin=client for the endpoint view and sample_origin=proxy for route view. weird.
wei: Can you paste the dashboard query? My hypothesis: we're mixing samples from different sampling policies during merge.
maya: Query from console: ```SELECT percentile(99, latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND time>now()-15m``` Route rollup does a different sample: `sample_by=route_weighted` in the rollup config.
alex: That mismatch will definitely alter tail metrics. route-weighted sampling can bias p99 if canary is small but high-latency.
priyanka: Also check quotas/fallback: if canary breached per-route quota we might be falling back to a slower instance class. deploy-bot: Canary deployment 2026-03-21T09:41:00Z -> weight 5% applied to route v2.
jon: telemetry-bot posted recent sample counts: total_count(endpoint) = 12k, total_count(route_v2) = 600, route_v2_high_latency_count=48 (8%). matches spike.
wei: So root cause likely: route-level rollup includes the tiny high-latency canary bucket, pushing route p99 up; endpoint-level query uses global sampling (client side) that under-samples the canary. two different sampling origins -> divergent percentiles.
maya: Agreed. UX ask: console should show provenance next to each percentile (client-sample vs route-rollup vs backend-tdigest) so you can see why numbers differ.
alex: +1. Also we need a small surgical fix: when route weights are <1% show a warning that rollup p99 may be unstable.
priyanka: For canaries I prefer deterministic sampling (include 100% of canary requests in rollups) until weight>threshold. That gives sane visibility.
jon: Implementation note: deterministic sampling for canary increases storage cost. Could we do a short-lived separate rollup table keyed by rollout_id? then expire after 24h.
wei: Or add a 'canary_provenance' flag in telemetry events so queries can easily filter. Both feasible.
maya: Action items: 1) telemetry: add provenance tag and emit explicit rollout_id (wei) 2) console: show sampling provenance badge + hover explainer (alex) 3) rollout: change canary sampling policy to deterministic up to 1% weight or use ephemeral rollup (priyanka) 4) docs: add a short note in rollouts UX about percentile variance (jon).
priyanka: I'll pilot deterministic canary-preserve for the next 24h and watch cost.
telemetry-bot: metric: canary_preserve_enabled=true for rollout v2 at 4751234567.
alex: Quick UX wire: small question — badge text should be "sampled-by: route-rollup" or abbreviate? prefer full text + tooltip.
jon: I'll add a tooltip copy. Also let's add a small debug panel to show raw sample counts beneath the percentile so SREs don't have to run queries.
maya: Thanks all. ping me once telemetry change is deployed and we'll re-evaluate p99 after 15m. :thumbsup:
